title: Risk scenarios
subject: PSHE
source: Written for pshe/y8 lesson 7 (Risk scenarios (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 7: Making safe choices and saying no. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Exit strategies
points: Agree a code word with parents
Have a charged phone and a contact
Leave a group chat that turns bad

questions.q: A stranger online offers you free game credits if you click a link and log in.
questions.a: Stop: too good to be true. Think: it could steal your account. Choose: do not click; tell a parent. Exit: block and report.

questions.q: A friend wants to cycle home in the dark with no lights.
questions.a: Stop. Think: drivers cannot see you. Choose: walk the bike, or call a parent. Exit: 'I'll get a lift, see you tomorrow.'

questions.q: You are at a friend's house and their older cousin starts showing a video you know is not appropriate.
questions.a: Stop. Think: you do not want to see it. Choose: say no. Exit: 'I need to call my mum', leave the room, and tell a parent.

questions.q: Someone in a group chat says to meet at a quiet canal path after dark.
questions.a: Stop. Think: unsafe place and time. Choose: say no. Exit: suggest daytime at a busy place, with a parent's permission.

keywords.def: what happens as a result of a choice
clear and respectful about what you will and will not do
a plan to leave a situation safely

questions.q: Use stop, think, choose for: 'A friend dares you to cross a busy road.'
questions.a: Stop; risk of injury; choose to refuse and walk to a crossing.

questions.q: Core: Risk scenarios (pupil PDF): apply stop, think, choose to each and write an exit strategy.
Extend: In the portal response box, write a reflection: who would you talk to after a risky situation, and why?
questions.a: Names a trusted adult and explains they can help.

questions.q: An online friend you have never met asks to meet alone. Safest choice?
options: Say no and tell a parent
Go with a friend your age
questions.a: B) Say no and tell a parent. People online may not be who they say; a parent must know and decide.

questions.q: Assertive means... A) shouting B) clear, calm and respectful C) agreeing to everything
Big question: how do you decide quickly when something feels wrong?
questions.a: Stop, think about consequences, choose the safe option, tell someone.
